consistency_argument.question: why can 1322 same-height centreline crossings (distance 0) coexist with 0 geometric violations?
consistency_argument.answer: Because the two rules act on disjoint partitions of the pair set. Same-physical-height flat/flat pairs are governed ONLY by the original strict D56 2-D rule (0.080 mm centreline clearance) which explicitly preserves genuine transverse crossings with angle >= 5 deg inside a local window; that rule is part of the frozen baseline contract (D56Index(crossing_policy="strict"), already used by the frozen 2409-crossing baseline), not a G4 addition. Pairs on different physical heights are governed by the 50 um 3-D rule, and such pairs can never have distance 0 (|dz| >= 0.050 mm); the 50 um rule therefore never "sees" the same-height crossings. All crossing events are genuine (angle >= 5 deg, interior, no overlap/tangency/double-cross), so no event falls into the clearance-violation category.
disjoint_rules: same physical height flat-flat <=> 2-D D56 0.08 mm + legal transverse crossing exemption
different physical height flat-flat <=> |dz| >= 0.05 mm (distance is bounded below by the layer pitch, XY overlap legal)
anything involving a transition <=> true 3-D centreline distance >= 0.05 mm (no crossing exemption)

contradiction_analysis.statement: The contract as codified in this repository does NOT require every centreline pair to be >= 50 um: same-height flat pairs use the 0.08 mm D56 2-D rule with a documented legal-crossing exemption, and only cross-height / transition-related pairs use the 50 um 3-D rule. Therefore the audited result is consistent with the code contract.
contradiction_analysis.residual_risk: IF the original written physical contract (task book) is meant to be a global "all centreline pairs >= 50 um with no exception" rule, then the 1322 legal crossings (distance exactly 0) would be 1322 hard violations and a genuine contradiction exists. This audit does NOT silently extend or create any exemption: the exemption is the pre-existing frozen D56 strict policy. The requirement-level interpretation must be confirmed by the project owner before the legal crossings are quoted as compliant.
